title: Zod & Schema Validation
description: Runtime schema validation with Zod — parse, infer, compose, and transform with full type safety.

challenges.title: Why Zod over manual validation
challenges.description:
What does Zod give you that manual validation (like the parseConfig from topic 09) does not?

  import { z } from 'zod'
  const ConfigSchema = z.object({ host: z.string(), port: z.number() })
  type Config = z.infer<typeof ConfigSchema>
challenges.whyMatters: Zod eliminates the gap between your TypeScript type and your runtime validator — they are the same thing. Manual validators drift from the type over time.
hints: z.infer derives the TypeScript type from the schema — one source of truth

choices.label: Zod is faster at runtime than manual checks
Zod derives the TypeScript type from the schema automatically — type and validator are always in sync, and error messages are detailed by default
Zod works at compile time; manual validation works at runtime
Zod replaces TypeScript's type system entirely

challenges.title: parse vs safeParse
challenges.whyMatters: safeParse is preferred in production tooling — it lets you handle validation errors gracefully instead of crashing with an uncaught exception.
hints: parse throws on failure; safeParse returns a discriminated union result

choices.label: parse throws a ZodError on failure; safeParse returns { success: true, data } or { success: false, error }
safeParse is slower because it does extra checks
parse returns undefined on failure; safeParse throws

challenges.title: Zod schema types
challenges.description:
Match each Zod method to what it validates:

  z.string().min(1)       → ?
  z.number().int().min(1) → ?
  z.enum(['a', 'b'])      → ?
  z.array(z.string())     → ?
  z.optional(z.string())  → ?
challenges.whyMatters: Knowing the Zod vocabulary lets you build schemas as fast as you can write TypeScript types.
hints: Zod's fluent API chains validators — each method adds a constraint

choices.label: non-empty string · positive integer · 'a'|'b' literal · string[] · string|undefined
string · number · union · tuple · nullable string
all return any — Zod is not type-safe
string · float · string · array · required string

challenges.title: Write a Zod config schema
challenges.description:
Write a Zod schema for this config and derive the TypeScript type from it:

- `host`: non-empty string
- `port`: integer between 1 and 65535
- `logLevel`: one of 'debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error'
- `workers`: positive integer, optional, defaults to 1
- `tags`: array of strings, optional, defaults to []

Export:
- `AppConfigSchema` — the Zod schema
- `AppConfig` — the inferred TypeScript type (use z.infer)
- `parseAppConfig(raw: unknown): AppConfig` — uses safeParse, throws with Zod's error message if invalid
challenges.whyMatters: This replaces 60 lines of manual validation from topic 09 with ~10 lines of Zod. This is the pattern you'll use in every new service.
hints: Use the string schema and chain a minimum-length validator to reject empty strings
Require an integer and chain both a minimum and maximum constraint to cover the valid port range
Use the Zod enum schema and pass the four allowed level strings as an array literal
Chain integer, positive, optional, and default validators in that order — the default fills in the value when the field is absent

challenges.title: Schema composition
challenges.whyMatters: Schema composition mirrors what utility types do at the type level — Zod brings the same power to the runtime layer.
hints: extend adds fields, pick selects fields, partial makes all optional, merge combines two schemas

choices.label: extend adds port · pick keeps only id · partial makes all optional · merge combines both schemas
All four are identical to extend
partial makes fields required · pick removes fields
merge overwrites conflicting fields with the right schema

challenges.title: Schema transforms and refinements
challenges.description:
Write Zod schemas with transforms and refinements:

1. `PortSchema` — accepts a string or number, transforms to number, validates it's 1–65535
   - `z.union([z.string(), z.number()])` → transform → refine

2. `UrlSchema` — string that must start with 'http://' or 'https://'
   - Use `.refine()` with a descriptive message

3. `EnvSchema` — an object schema for environment variables (all string inputs):
   - `PORT`: use PortSchema
   - `API_URL`: use UrlSchema  
   - `LOG_LEVEL`: transform to lowercase, then validate against allowed values
   - `DEBUG`: string '0'|'1', transform to boolean

Export each schema and the inferred `Env` type.
challenges.whyMatters: Transforms are essential for env var parsing — everything comes in as a string and needs to become the right type. Refinements catch business-rule violations that basic types can't express.
hints: Accept either a string or number input, transform to a number, then refine to validate the port range — chain all three steps
Start with a string schema and add a refinement that checks both protocol prefixes — provide a descriptive message in the refinement options
Add a transform to the DEBUG field that converts the string to a boolean — decide on the truthy string value and return the comparison result

challenges.title: Build a validated config loader with Zod
challenges.description:
Build a complete config loading system:

`DeploymentSchema` — validates a deployment manifest:
- `name`: non-empty string
- `image`: string matching pattern `name:tag` (use refine + regex)
- `replicas`: integer 1–20
- `env`: optional record of string to string
- `resources`: optional object with `cpu` (string) and `memory` (string)

`loadDeployments(raw: unknown): Deployment[]` — validates an array of deployment manifests, throws with all validation errors if any fail (not just the first)

`validateAndSummarize(raw: unknown): string` — returns `'N valid deployments: name1, name2, ...'` or throws with error details.

Export `DeploymentSchema`, `Deployment` (inferred type), and both functions.
challenges.whyMatters: Validating arrays of deployment manifests — from YAML, JSON API, or stdin — is a daily software engineering task. Collecting all errors (not just the first) is critical for good developer experience.
hints: Use a regex method to enforce the name:tag format — the pattern must match a name segment, a colon, and a tag segment with allowed characters
Model the env field as a record schema where both keys and values are strings
Wrap DeploymentSchema in an array schema to validate a list of deployments — safeParse will validate every element
The ZodError contains an array of individual issue objects — each has a message field; map over them and join to produce a single error string
